learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of analyzing and solving systems of linear equations.
Apply analytical and numerical methods to model and solve engineering problems represented as linear systems.
Implement solving algorithms in a suitable computational environment.
Know and understand the theoretical foundations of linear algebra applied to systems of linear equations.
Have notions of sensitivity and conditioning of linear systems.
Be able to apply analytical methods (exact resolution) and numerical methods (LU, QR decomposition, etc.) to solve linear systems.
Implement practical algorithm solutions in software environments such as Scilab or Matlab.
Be aware of the significance of linear systems in engineering and modeling fields.
Acknowledge the rigor required to interpret the results of numerical solutions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to linear systems and matrix algebra.
Direct numerical methods (LU decomposition, QR, etc.).
Indirect numerical method (iterative method: Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, etc.)
Solving exercises and implementing algorithms in a software environment using Matlab or Scilab.
teaching_methods: Practical exercises using Scilab/Matlab for algorithm implementation
bibliography: G. Allaire, S.M. Kaber, Algèbre linéaire numérique, Ellipses, 2002.
F. Rotella, I. Zambettakis, Traitement des systèmes linéaires, Ellipses, 2015.
G.H. Golub, C.F. Van Loan, Matrix Computations, Johns Hopkins University Press, 1996.
degree: Titre d'ingénieur ENIT (cycle ingénieur, semestres 5-10; orientación mecánica/producción)
